title: PROSE-102 reports no verb in plain sentences whose verb it does not know
foundBy: session agent working in the simple-tools-demo repository, which runs a three member campaign at the pinned build of 2026-09-17, while writing a README and ledger records under `cs-lint prose`
details:
`PROSE-102` flags a sentence as `no verb: an epigram, not a sentence` when the sentence has an ordinary finite verb. Five of these eight sentences fail at the current head of `main`:

```
It installs the tools from two places.              fails
The orchestrator designs the page and commits that design.   fails
The viewer draws the timeline.                      fails
It looked like a slow model.                        fails
Two things stand in the way.                        fails
The tool exits when the run is over.                passes
The check looks for a reply every thirty seconds.   passes
The tool runs when the file changes.                passes
```

The failing verbs are `installs`, `designs`, `draws`, `looked` and `stand`. Each sentence is the plain expository kind the rule exists to encourage.

The cost is that the writer learns the verb list rather than the rule. In one session this rule fired seven times, and every fix was to swap a correct verb for one the linter knew. `It installs the tools from two places` was rewritten as `The tools come from two places`. Nothing about the first sentence was wrong.

The rule also lints ledger records, so a record's wording gets bent the same way. Five sentences in the records filed beside this one were rejected too. Their verbs were `mentions`, `killed`, `worked`, `honours` and `became`, as in `Recovery worked, so the campaign still ended.`

To reproduce, put those sentences in a `README.md` on lines of their own, separated by blank lines, and run `cs-lint prose --root <dir>`.
